skills.description: Use when raw DSF fluorescence-versus-temperature data from a multi-well plate must be compared across wells whose absolute fluorescence intensities differ, i.e. when each melting curve needs per-curve min-max normalization prior to smoothing or Tm analysis.
skills.name: per-well-plate-data-processing
skills.search_text: per-well-plate-data-processing Use when raw DSF fluorescence-versus-temperature data from a multi-well plate must be compared across wells whose absolute fluorescence intensities differ, i.e. when each melting curve needs per-curve min-max normalization prior to smoothing or Tm analysis. The fluorescence data are not melting curves from a DSF plate experiment and per-curve 0–1 rescaling would be meaningless Each melting curve is already min-max normalized to the 0–1 range, so re-applying Equation 1 would not change values The goal is absolute fluorescence-intensity comparison across wells, where the per-curve rescaling of Equation 1 would destroy the intensity information http://edamontology.org/topic_3369 Applies SimpleDSFviewer's melting-curve (MC) normalization per well to differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF) fluorescence-versus-temperature data: subtracting each curve's minimum and dividing by its (max − min) range (Equation 1) to rescale every MC into the 0–1 interval before smoothing and Tm analysis. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pro.3703
skills.summary: Applies SimpleDSFviewer's melting-curve (MC) normalization per well to differential scanning fluorimetry (DSF) fluorescence-versus-temperature data: subtracting each curve's minimum and dividing by its (max − min) range (Equation 1) to rescale every MC into the 0–1 interval before smoothing and Tm analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The fluorescence data are not melting curves from a DSF plate experiment and per-curve 0–1 rescaling would be meaningless Each melting curve is already min-max normalized to the 0–1 range, so re-applying Equation 1 would not change values The goal is absolute fluorescence-intensity comparison across wells, where the per-curve rescaling of Equation 1 would destroy the intensity information

skills.description: Use when you have normalized, smoothed DSF melting curves per well on a uniform temperature ramp and need derivative curves whose peaks locate each well's melting temperature (Tm).
skills.name: per-well-timeseries-processing
skills.search_text: per-well-timeseries-processing Use when you have normalized, smoothed DSF melting curves per well on a uniform temperature ramp and need derivative curves whose peaks locate each well's melting temperature (Tm). Input melting curves are raw and have not yet been normalized and smoothed by the upstream SimpleDSFviewer step, since Equation 2 is defined on the normalized, smoothed MCs The DSF acquisition has non-uniform temperature increments, so the constant Δt in the central-difference denominator is invalid The goal is Tm analysis directly on raw fluorescence rather than derivative-curve-based peak identification Compute per-well first-derivative curves (FDCs) from DSF melting curves using SimpleDSFviewer's central-difference Equation 2, FDC = (MC(n+1) − MC(n−1)) / (2Δt), then normalize the FDCs exactly like the MCs so derivative amplitudes are comparable across wells. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pro.3703
skills.summary: Compute per-well first-derivative curves (FDCs) from DSF melting curves using SimpleDSFviewer's central-difference Equation 2, FDC = (MC(n+1) − MC(n−1)) / (2Δt), then normalize the FDCs exactly like the MCs so derivative amplitudes are comparable across wells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input melting curves are raw and have not yet been normalized and smoothed by the upstream SimpleDSFviewer step, since Equation 2 is defined on the normalized, smoothed MCs The DSF acquisition has non-uniform temperature increments, so the constant Δt in the central-difference denominator is invalid The goal is Tm analysis directly on raw fluorescence rather than derivative-curve-based peak identification

skills.description: Use when filtering isobarically-labeled (iTRAQ/TMT/TMTpro) peptide quantifications from SPS-MS3, RTS-MS3, or MS2 runs with IsobaricQuant QC scores and a defensible, dataset-specific starting cutoff is needed before protein-level quantification.
skills.name: percentile-cutoff-optimization
skills.search_text: percentile-cutoff-optimization Use when filtering isobarically-labeled (iTRAQ/TMT/TMTpro) peptide quantifications from SPS-MS3, RTS-MS3, or MS2 runs with IsobaricQuant QC scores and a defensible, dataset-specific starting cutoff is needed before protein-level quantification. When the acquisition method limits PSMs per protein (e.g., the PISA RTS-MS3 method capped at 2 PSMs per protein), which 'significantly limited the possibility of filtering peptides' When a single universal cutoff is expected to transfer across datasets — the article states optimal score and cutoff 'will be dataset-dependent' When preserving maximum peptide observations across multiple labeled sample sets is the priority, since stringent filtering 'can lead to substantial loss of peptide observations' http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 A data-driven strategy for choosing IsobaricQuant QC-score filtering cutoffs (e.g., peptideTopXIntensityFromTotalScore with topX = 10, peptideIntensityScore, msnTotalSignal) by starting from the 25th percentile of each dataset's score distribution, then adjusting per dataset to balance improved CVs against peptide-observation loss. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.202100253
skills.summary: A data-driven strategy for choosing IsobaricQuant QC-score filtering cutoffs (e.g., peptideTopXIntensityFromTotalScore with topX = 10, peptideIntensityScore, msnTotalSignal) by starting from the 25th percentile of each dataset's score distribution, then adjusting per dataset to balance improved CVs against peptide-observation loss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the acquisition method limits PSMs per protein (e.g., the PISA RTS-MS3 method capped at 2 PSMs per protein), which 'significantly limited the possibility of filtering peptides' When a single universal cutoff is expected to transfer across datasets — the article states optimal score and cutoff 'will be dataset-dependent' When preserving maximum peptide observations across multiple labeled sample sets is the priority, since stringent filtering 'can lead to substantial loss of peptide observations'

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether peptide identifications from immunopeptidomics searches (e.g., DeepRescore *_pep_final.tsv outputs or 1%-FDR-filtered search-engine peptide lists) are enriched for predicted MHC binders using binding-affinity prediction tools.
skills.name: percentile-rank-binder-classification
skills.search_text: percentile-rank-binder-classification Use when evaluating whether peptide identifications from immunopeptidomics searches (e.g., DeepRescore *_pep_final.tsv outputs or 1%-FDR-filtered search-engine peptide lists) are enriched for predicted MHC binders using binding-affinity prediction tools. When peptides fall outside length 8-11 — the paper restricts the binding-affinity evaluation to this range (it covered at least 75% of identified peptides), so results on other lengths are out of scope When no HLA allele information is available for the sample — the percentile rank scoring requires assigning alleles (per-allele best rank for multi-allelic D1, A*11:01 for D2) When the goal is to evaluate PSM-level or spectrum-level quality rather than predicted MHC binding of peptide sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Classifies MHC-presented peptides as binders by applying a percentile-rank-score threshold (<=2%) to NetMHCpan, MHCflurry, and HLAthena binding-affinity predictions, and compares binder ratios across peptide identification methods (Comet, MS-GF+, X!Tandem, MaxQuant, vs. DeepRescore-rescored). proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201900334
skills.summary: Classifies MHC-presented peptides as binders by applying a percentile-rank-score threshold (<=2%) to NetMHCpan, MHCflurry, and HLAthena binding-affinity predictions, and compares binder ratios across peptide identification methods (Comet, MS-GF+, X!Tandem, MaxQuant, vs. DeepRescore-rescored).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When peptides fall outside length 8-11 — the paper restricts the binding-affinity evaluation to this range (it covered at least 75% of identified peptides), so results on other lengths are out of scope When no HLA allele information is available for the sample — the percentile rank scoring requires assigning alleles (per-allele best rank for multi-allelic D1, A*11:01 for D2) When the goal is to evaluate PSM-level or spectrum-level quality rather than predicted MHC binding of peptide sequences

skills.description: Use when FT-ICR MS-derived DOM molecular compositional data (samples x molecular formula presence/absence and relative abundance) must be compared between predefined groups, e.g., climatic regions, to test compositional similarity.
skills.name: permanova-regional-composition-testing
skills.search_text: permanova-regional-composition-testing Use when FT-ICR MS-derived DOM molecular compositional data (samples x molecular formula presence/absence and relative abundance) must be compared between predefined groups, e.g., climatic regions, to test compositional similarity. Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra rather than a processed formula-by-sample compositional table (traits/class assignment must be done first with iDOM's basic functions) The goal is quantifying DOM assembly processes, dark matter effects, or DOM-microbe networks (use commProc, iDME, or H2 instead) Groups have unequal dispersion that could confound PERMANOVA significance (differences in multivariate spread can mimic compositional differences) Quantifies whether dissolved organic matter (DOM) molecular composition differs between groupings (e.g., subtropical vs temperate regions) by computing sample-by-sample dissimilarity matrices with iDOM's commDis and testing them with PERMANOVA (vegan::adonis2). proteomics/v1 10.1002/mlf2.70002
skills.summary: Quantifies whether dissolved organic matter (DOM) molecular composition differs between groupings (e.g., subtropical vs temperate regions) by computing sample-by-sample dissimilarity matrices with iDOM's commDis and testing them with PERMANOVA (vegan::adonis2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FT-ICR MS spectra rather than a processed formula-by-sample compositional table (traits/class assignment must be done first with iDOM's basic functions) The goal is quantifying DOM assembly processes, dark matter effects, or DOM-microbe networks (use commProc, iDME, or H2 instead) Groups have unequal dispersion that could confound PERMANOVA significance (differences in multivariate spread can mimic compositional differences)

skills.description: Use when a task requires predicting 3D PET images (e.g., av45 amyloid PET) from paired T1w/FLAIR MRI volumes at 256x256x256 resolution, with quantitative image-quality benchmarking.
skills.name: pet-image-synthesis-from-mri
skills.search_text: pet-image-synthesis-from-mri Use when a task requires predicting 3D PET images (e.g., av45 amyloid PET) from paired T1w/FLAIR MRI volumes at 256x256x256 resolution, with quantitative image-quality benchmarking. The target modality is a quantitative map (e.g., DTI-derived FA or MD metrics) where normalizing voxel intensities to 0-1 would destroy the quantitative value of the metrics — the paper notes normalization negatively affects quantitative metrics and should be avoided for synthesizing quantitative modalities The input images are low-resolution or 2D slices and an end-to-end 3D pipeline at 256x256x256 is not feasible — SC-GAN requires heavy GPU memory and lengthy training, which is its main limitation The task is superresolution of diffusion MRI with different acquisition protocols rather than cross-modal PET synthesis from T1w/FLAIR MRI http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3334 Synthesize 3D amyloid PET images from multimodal MRI (T1w and FLAIR) using SC-GAN, a 3D self-attention conditional GAN with spectral normalization, trained on the ADNI-3 cohort and benchmarked against 2D cGAN, 3D cGAN, and Att cGAN baselines using NRMSE, peak SNR, and SSIM. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mrm.28819
skills.summary: Synthesize 3D amyloid PET images from multimodal MRI (T1w and FLAIR) using SC-GAN, a 3D self-attention conditional GAN with spectral normalization, trained on the ADNI-3 cohort and benchmarked against 2D cGAN, 3D cGAN, and Att cGAN baselines using NRMSE, peak SNR, and SSIM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target modality is a quantitative map (e.g., DTI-derived FA or MD metrics) where normalizing voxel intensities to 0-1 would destroy the quantitative value of the metrics — the paper notes normalization negatively affects quantitative metrics and should be avoided for synthesizing quantitative modalities The input images are low-resolution or 2D slices and an end-to-end 3D pipeline at 256x256x256 is not feasible — SC-GAN requires heavy GPU memory and lengthy training, which is its main limitation The task is superresolution of diffusion MRI with different acquisition protocols rather than cross-modal PET synthesis from T1w/FLAIR MRI

skills.description: Use when amyloid PET images must be aligned to T1w MRI for regional SUVR quantification, or when validating synthesized PET against measured (ground-truth) PET across atlas regions in ADNI-type data.
skills.name: pet-mri-coregistration
skills.search_text: pet-mri-coregistration Use when amyloid PET images must be aligned to T1w MRI for regional SUVR quantification, or when validating synthesized PET against measured (ground-truth) PET across atlas regions in ADNI-type data. PET images are already co-registered to T1w space with the brain mask applied and only raw voxel-wise synthesis (e.g., SC-GAN training) is needed — skip straight to Z-score/min-max normalization and training The target modality is quantitative DTI (FA/MD) — the article notes normalization negatively affects quantitative metric values, so the min-max rescaling step in this PET workflow should be avoided there Images have uncorrected nonuniform field inhomogeneity — run N4ITK correction (ANTs) first, as done in the article's preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3384 Co-registers amyloid PET images (e.g., ADNI av45) onto T1w MRI and computes regional standard uptake value ratios (SUVR) using the UC Berkeley PET methodology over the 110 Desikan-Killiany subcortical and cortical regions, enabling direct comparison of synthesized versus measured PET uptake. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mrm.28819
skills.summary: Co-registers amyloid PET images (e.g., ADNI av45) onto T1w MRI and computes regional standard uptake value ratios (SUVR) using the UC Berkeley PET methodology over the 110 Desikan-Killiany subcortical and cortical regions, enabling direct comparison of synthesized versus measured PET uptake.
skills.when_to_use_negative: PET images are already co-registered to T1w space with the brain mask applied and only raw voxel-wise synthesis (e.g., SC-GAN training) is needed — skip straight to Z-score/min-max normalization and training The target modality is quantitative DTI (FA/MD) — the article notes normalization negatively affects quantitative metric values, so the min-max rescaling step in this PET workflow should be avoided there Images have uncorrected nonuniform field inhomogeneity — run N4ITK correction (ANTs) first, as done in the article's preprocessing

skills.description: Use when regional amyloid-PET uptake must be quantified as SUVR over cortical/subcortical parcellations and compared between measured PET and MRI-synthesized PET.
skills.name: pet-surv-quantification
skills.search_text: pet-surv-quantification Use when regional amyloid-PET uptake must be quantified as SUVR over cortical/subcortical parcellations and compared between measured PET and MRI-synthesized PET. You need voxel-level image-quality metrics (nRMSE, peak SNR, SSIM) rather than regionally averaged uptake ratios You are synthesizing quantitative DTI metrics (FA, MD), where the article warns that min-max normalization negatively affects the quantitative value of the metrics and should be avoided No co-registered T1w image is available, so no reliable brain mask or FreeSurfer parcellation can be derived Quantifies regional amyloid-PET uptake as standard uptake value ratios (SUVR) per Desikan-Killiany region by co-registering PET to T1w MRI, applying a T1w-derived brain mask, and parcellating with FreeSurfer 5.3.0. Enables direct paired comparison of SUVRs from measured (ground-truth) vs synthesized (e.g., SC-GAN) PET images. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mrm.28819
skills.summary: Quantifies regional amyloid-PET uptake as standard uptake value ratios (SUVR) per Desikan-Killiany region by co-registering PET to T1w MRI, applying a T1w-derived brain mask, and parcellating with FreeSurfer 5.3.0. Enables direct paired comparison of SUVRs from measured (ground-truth) vs synthesized (e.g., SC-GAN) PET images.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need voxel-level image-quality metrics (nRMSE, peak SNR, SSIM) rather than regionally averaged uptake ratios You are synthesizing quantitative DTI metrics (FA, MD), where the article warns that min-max normalization negatively affects the quantitative value of the metrics and should be avoided No co-registered T1w image is available, so no reliable brain mask or FreeSurfer parcellation can be derived

skills.description: Use when an X-ray protein–ligand complex structure and its BANΔIT-normalized B'-factor/ΔB' profiles are available and a structure-based pharmacophore model should be annotated with protein-mobility (B'-factor) support for drug design.
skills.name: pharmacophore-feature-annotation
skills.search_text: pharmacophore-feature-annotation Use when an X-ray protein–ligand complex structure and its BANΔIT-normalized B'-factor/ΔB' profiles are available and a structure-based pharmacophore model should be annotated with protein-mobility (B'-factor) support for drug design. No X-ray B'-factor data are available for the protein (e.g. only NMR or predicted structures), since the method relies on B'-factor profile normalization from X-ray protein structures The goal is conventional ligand- or shape-based pharmacophore generation that does not require B'-factor/ΔB' interaction-quality annotation Builds a B'-factor-supported pharmacophore model by mapping BANΔIT-normalized B'-factor/ΔB' residue profiles onto binding-site residues of an X-ray structure and annotating pharmacophore feature types (e.g. hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor, hydrophobic, aromatic) with their B'-factor support, as demonstrated for SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors. proteomics/v1 10.1002/minf.202000144
skills.summary: Builds a B'-factor-supported pharmacophore model by mapping BANΔIT-normalized B'-factor/ΔB' residue profiles onto binding-site residues of an X-ray structure and annotating pharmacophore feature types (e.g. hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor, hydrophobic, aromatic) with their B'-factor support, as demonstrated for SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No X-ray B'-factor data are available for the protein (e.g. only NMR or predicted structures), since the method relies on B'-factor profile normalization from X-ray protein structures The goal is conventional ligand- or shape-based pharmacophore generation that does not require B'-factor/ΔB' interaction-quality annotation

skills.description: Use when a phase-contrast MRI pulse design must null flow-encoding moments in minimum time T, and the dependence of minimum T and compute time on raster time dt and added PNS/moment constraints is of interest.
skills.name: phase-contrast-mri-gradient-design
skills.search_text: phase-contrast-mri-gradient-design Use when a phase-contrast MRI pulse design must null flow-encoding moments in minimum time T, and the dependence of minimum T and compute time on raster time dt and added PNS/moment constraints is of interest. The task is optimizing readout trajectories or non-phase-contrast slice-select gradients — the article notes the GrOpt toolbox has not been used to optimize readout trajectories or slice-select gradients in general Longer gradient waveforms such as multiecho turbo-spin-echo sequences are targeted — the article notes the choice of N and dt may need adjustment there The design goal is b-value maximization or duty-cycle minimization for diffusion rather than flow-encoding moment nulling for phase contrast Designs time-optimal phase-contrast MRI slice-selection and flow-encoding gradient waveforms with GrOpt, searching over waveform durations T and raster times dt under Gmax, slew-rate, gradient-moment-nulling, and optional PNS constraints, and benchmarks compute time per configuration. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mrm.28384
skills.summary: Designs time-optimal phase-contrast MRI slice-selection and flow-encoding gradient waveforms with GrOpt, searching over waveform durations T and raster times dt under Gmax, slew-rate, gradient-moment-nulling, and optional PNS constraints, and benchmarks compute time per configuration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is optimizing readout trajectories or non-phase-contrast slice-select gradients — the article notes the GrOpt toolbox has not been used to optimize readout trajectories or slice-select gradients in general Longer gradient waveforms such as multiecho turbo-spin-echo sequences are targeted — the article notes the choice of N and dt may need adjustment there The design goal is b-value maximization or duty-cycle minimization for diffusion rather than flow-encoding moment nulling for phase contrast

skills.summary: Designs the Ant Colony Optimization pheromone-update cycle used by Popitam to parse a combinatorial MS/MS spectrum graph, progressively emphasizing graph sections that match each theoretical peptide sequence from a database.

skills.name: phosphosite-label-annotation
skills.search_text: phosphosite-label-annotation Use when classifier phosphosite predictions show a precision-recall tradeoff with many predicted false positives, and an experimentally derived phosphosite database (e.g. qPTMplants) is available to relabel matching false positives as inferred positives. You need calibrated per-site probability scores rather than alignment-based label relabeling — DIAMOND inference supplements classification but does not replace model probabilities The query phosphosites have no plausible homologs in the experimentally derived database (e.g. divergent species with no qPTMplants coverage), since the step depends on pairwise sequence similarity Tyr phosphosite analysis where the article found the step 'not as informative at predicting inferred positives compared to false positives, possibly due to higher label imbalance' http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 A supplementary DIAMOND pairwise sequence-alignment step that annotates PhosBoost (or other classifier) phosphosite predictions by relabeling predicted false positives that match experimentally derived phosphosites as inferred positives, reducing label uncertainty and boosting effective recall. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pld3.554
skills.summary: A supplementary DIAMOND pairwise sequence-alignment step that annotates PhosBoost (or other classifier) phosphosite predictions by relabeling predicted false positives that match experimentally derived phosphosites as inferred positives, reducing label uncertainty and boosting effective recall.

skills.description: Use when preparing candidate phosphosites from protein sequences for sequence-alignment-based inference, e.g. relabeling predicted false positives as inferred positives via DIAMOND alignment to experimentally derived phosphosite databases.
skills.name: phosphosite-peptide-window-extraction
skills.search_text: phosphosite-peptide-window-extraction Use when preparing candidate phosphosites from protein sequences for sequence-alignment-based inference, e.g. relabeling predicted false positives as inferred positives via DIAMOND alignment to experimentally derived phosphosite databases. Protein sequences contain missing or non-canonical amino acids, or the phosphorylation position does not match the protein sequence — these proteins/sites are discarded per the article's filter steps before window extraction. The goal is classifier training rather than alignment-based inference — PhosBoost training uses full residue embedding vectors, not extracted 31-residue peptide windows for alignment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0601 http://edamontology.org/topic_3510 Extracts fixed-length (31-residue) peptide windows centered on candidate Ser/Thr/Tyr phosphosites from protein FASTA sequences, so that phosphorylation sites can be compared via pairwise sequence alignment (e.g. DIAMOND) rather than relying on classifier probabilities alone. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pld3.554
skills.summary: Extracts fixed-length (31-residue) peptide windows centered on candidate Ser/Thr/Tyr phosphosites from protein FASTA sequences, so that phosphorylation sites can be compared via pairwise sequence alignment (e.g. DIAMOND) rather than relying on classifier probabilities alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Protein sequences contain missing or non-canonical amino acids, or the phosphorylation position does not match the protein sequence — these proteins/sites are discarded per the article's filter steps before window extraction. The goal is classifier training rather than alignment-based inference — PhosBoost training uses full residue embedding vectors, not extracted 31-residue peptide windows for alignment.

skills.description: Use when you have amino acid sequences of a protein family (e.g., FASTA of homologs across many genomes) and need an evolutionary tree relating them, starting from an unaligned FASTA.
skills.name: phylogenetic-tree-inference
skills.search_text: phylogenetic-tree-inference Use when you have amino acid sequences of a protein family (e.g., FASTA of homologs across many genomes) and need an evolutionary tree relating them, starting from an unaligned FASTA. Your input is already an alignment or a finished Newick tree — re-running MUSCLE alignment is unnecessary and FastTree would need the aligned FASTA, not a tree You need exhaustive maximum-likelihood inference with bootstrap support or model selection (e.g., RAxML/IQ-TREE use cases) — FastTree provides an approximate ML topology only The goal is structural comparison rather than sequence-based phylogeny — CBP60-DB uses TM-Align-based structural clustering for that purpose instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0084 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reconstructs a phylogeny of a protein family by feeding a MUSCLE-generated multiple sequence alignment (produced with MEGA11 configuration) into FastTree, yielding an approximate maximum-likelihood tree in Newick format. skills.summary: Reconstructs a phylogeny of a protein family by feeding a MUSCLE-generated multiple sequence alignment (produced with MEGA11 configuration) into FastTree, yielding an approximate maximum-likelihood tree in Newick format. skills.description: Use when ColabFold (AlphaFold2) has produced predicted 3D structures for protein sequences (e.g., a plant protein family like CBP60) and you need to capture and serialize the model's self-estimated confidence (pLDDT, PAE, pTM) for downstream validation, display, or clustering.
skills.name: plddt-pae-confidence-metric-extraction
skills.search_text: plddt-pae-confidence-metric-extraction Use when ColabFold (AlphaFold2) has produced predicted 3D structures for protein sequences (e.g., a plant protein family like CBP60) and you need to capture and serialize the model's self-estimated confidence (pLDDT, PAE, pTM) for downstream validation, display, or clustering. Input is raw, unaligned protein sequences with no predicted structure yet — run ColabFold first to generate the pLDDT/PAE data before extraction. You need experimentally determined (e.g., crystal or cryo-EM) structure quality metrics rather than AlphaFold2 self-estimated confidence — pLDDT/PAE are model-predicted, not experimental, measures. You only need structure similarity clustering rather than per-residue/pairwise confidence — use TM-Align-based clustering (as in CBP60-DB) instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_2828 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Extract per-residue pLDDT and pairwise PAE (plus pTM) confidence metrics from ColabFold/AlphaFold2 structural predictions and archive them as JSON alongside the predicted PDB/mmCIF structures, as done for the plant CBP60 proteins in CBP60-DB. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pld3.509
skills.summary: Extract per-residue pLDDT and pairwise PAE (plus pTM) confidence metrics from ColabFold/AlphaFold2 structural predictions and archive them as JSON alongside the predicted PDB/mmCIF structures, as done for the plant CBP60 proteins in CBP60-DB.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unaligned protein sequences with no predicted structure yet — run ColabFold first to generate the pLDDT/PAE data before extraction. You need experimentally determined (e.g., crystal or cryo-EM) structure quality metrics rather than AlphaFold2 self-estimated confidence — pLDDT/PAE are model-predicted, not experimental, measures. You only need structure similarity clustering rather than per-residue/pairwise confidence — use TM-Align-based clustering (as in CBP60-DB) instead.

skills.description: Use when a gradient waveform design task (e.g., phase-contrast slice-selection or flow encoding, diffusion encoding with moment nulling) must additionally satisfy a peripheral nerve stimulation limit, per Schulte et al or Hebrank et al models, in GrOpt.
skills.name: pns-constraint-waveform-design
skills.search_text: pns-constraint-waveform-design Use when a gradient waveform design task (e.g., phase-contrast slice-selection or flow encoding, diffusion encoding with moment nulling) must additionally satisfy a peripheral nerve stimulation limit, per Schulte et al or Hebrank et al models, in GrOpt. Designing readout trajectories or slice-select gradients — GrOpt has not been used to optimize those per the discussion When the waveform has no patient-comfort requirement — plain moment-nulling or eddy-current-nulling designs avoid the O(n^2.32) runtime penalty of the PNS constraint When a formal proof of time-optimality or convexity is required — with multiple constraints (PNS plus others) convexity is difficult to prove and brute-force optimality checks are computationally very expensive Design time-optimal MRI gradient waveforms in GrOpt while explicitly limiting peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS), using the Schulte et al or Hebrank et al PNS models as constraints inside the ADMM-based optimization. Adding the PNS constraint raises compute-time scaling relative to unconstrained waveform design, so this skill trades runtime for patient comfort. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mrm.28384
skills.summary: Design time-optimal MRI gradient waveforms in GrOpt while explicitly limiting peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS), using the Schulte et al or Hebrank et al PNS models as constraints inside the ADMM-based optimization. Adding the PNS constraint raises compute-time scaling relative to unconstrained waveform design, so this skill trades runtime for patient comfort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Designing readout trajectories or slice-select gradients — GrOpt has not been used to optimize those per the discussion When the waveform has no patient-comfort requirement — plain moment-nulling or eddy-current-nulling designs avoid the O(n^2.32) runtime penalty of the PNS constraint When a formal proof of time-optimality or convexity is required — with multiple constraints (PNS plus others) convexity is difficult to prove and brute-force optimality checks are computationally very expensive

skills.description: Use when FT-ICR MS molecular intensity data and microbial abundance tables are available and the goal is to test how positive vs. negative DOM-microbe interactions respond to an environmental treatment such as warming.
skills.name: positive-negative-interaction-partitioning
skills.search_text: positive-negative-interaction-partitioning Use when FT-ICR MS molecular intensity data and microbial abundance tables are available and the goal is to test how positive vs. negative DOM-microbe interactions respond to an environmental treatment such as warming. Input lacks paired DOM molecular and microbial taxon abundance data, so a bipartite DOM-microbe network cannot be constructed The question is DOM assemblage assembly or dark-matter effects rather than interaction specialization — use the commProc or iDME functions instead Only univariate DOM thermal response is needed — use the iCER indicator of compositional-level environmental response rather than bipartite network partitioning Partitions DOM-microbe bipartite co-occurrence networks into full, negative, and positive interaction networks and quantifies network-level standardized specialization (H2′) of each variant using the iDOM H2 function, so warming responses can be compared between cooperative and competitive interaction pools. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mlf2.70002
skills.summary: Partitions DOM-microbe bipartite co-occurrence networks into full, negative, and positive interaction networks and quantifies network-level standardized specialization (H2′) of each variant using the iDOM H2 function, so warming responses can be compared between cooperative and competitive interaction pools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input lacks paired DOM molecular and microbial taxon abundance data, so a bipartite DOM-microbe network cannot be constructed The question is DOM assemblage assembly or dark-matter effects rather than interaction specialization — use the commProc or iDME functions instead Only univariate DOM thermal response is needed — use the iCER indicator of compositional-level environmental response rather than bipartite network partitioning

skills.search_text: protein-hydrogen-bond-energy-calculation Use when backbone N, C, O, CA coordinates are available (e.g. PDB/mmCIF files like 3PTI, 155C, 2ADK) and donor-acceptor hydrogen bonds must be classified quantitatively by the DSSP energy rule. When the goal is secondary structure *prediction* from sequence — DSSP does not predict, it assigns from coordinates ('DSSP does not predict secondary structure') When solvent-side-chain or ligand-mediated hydrogen bonds are needed — this skill covers only backbone C=O / N-H pairs from the energy rule When proline residues are involved as donors — prolines lack an amide H and must be skipped http://edamontology.org/topic_0082 Implements the DSSP electrostatic hydrogen-bond definition: a Coulomb-type interaction energy E is computed for every backbone C=O/N-H pair from partial charges and a hydrogen bond is assigned when E < -0.5 kcal/mol. skills.description: Use when a set of protein sequence variants (e.g. from a BLAST search or a UniProt/Ensembl variant download) has been aligned with MUSCLE and per-position absolute and percent amino acid occurrence matrices are needed downstream of or alongside 3D structure conservation mapping.
skills.name: protein-sequence-conservation-quantification
skills.search_text: protein-sequence-conservation-quantification Use when a set of protein sequence variants (e.g. from a BLAST search or a UniProt/Ensembl variant download) has been aligned with MUSCLE and per-position absolute and percent amino acid occurrence matrices are needed downstream of or alongside 3D structure conservation mapping. The analysis goal is SNP variant frequency/type annotation rather than amino acid occurrence/conservation (scop3D's -var mode produces a different matrix annotating the protein sequence with frequency, variants and type of variant). No aligned set of variant sequences exists and only a single reference sequence is available — per-position occurrence counts require multiple variants. The goal is already-solved downstream output such as the modified PDB files with B-values replaced by percent conservation or entropy; this skill covers only the per-position occurrence matrices stage. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes per-position amino acid occurrence statistics from a multiple sequence alignment of protein variants, producing two text-file matrices that annotate the consensus sequence with absolute and relative (percent) abundances of each amino acid, as implemented in scop3D. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201400354
skills.summary: Computes per-position amino acid occurrence statistics from a multiple sequence alignment of protein variants, producing two text-file matrices that annotate the consensus sequence with absolute and relative (percent) abundances of each amino acid, as implemented in scop3D.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is SNP variant frequency/type annotation rather than amino acid occurrence/conservation (scop3D's -var mode produces a different matrix annotating the protein sequence with frequency, variants and type of variant). No aligned set of variant sequences exists and only a single reference sequence is available — per-position occurrence counts require multiple variants. The goal is already-solved downstream output such as the modified PDB files with B-values replaced by percent conservation or entropy; this skill covers only the per-position occurrence matrices stage.

skills.summary: Deduplicate protein FASTA datasets by clustering redundant sequences with CD-HIT at a 30% identity cutoff before feature extraction and model construction, as done for the plant R protein dataset (Wang et al. [9]) used by prPred-DRLF.

skills.description: Use when a published X-ray structure is available and BANΔIT-derived B'-factor/ΔB' residue profiles must be transferred onto binding-site residues to derive a B'-factor-supported pharmacophore model.

skills.search_text: protein-structure-data-mapping Use when a published X-ray structure is available and BANΔIT-derived B'-factor/ΔB' residue profiles must be transferred onto binding-site residues to derive a B'-factor-supported pharmacophore model. The input protein structure is not from X-ray crystallography — B'-factor/ΔB' profiles derive from X-ray B-factors and are not meaningful for NMR or cryo-EM-only models. skills.description: Use when reproducing DSSP static solvent exposure — number of water molecules in possible contact with each residue — from PDB/mmCIF atomic coordinates, or when benchmarking an accessible-surface-area implementation against the published Lee and Richards myoglobin values.
skills.name: rolling-probe-surface-integration
skills.search_text: rolling-probe-surface-integration Use when reproducing DSSP static solvent exposure — number of water molecules in possible contact with each residue — from PDB/mmCIF atomic coordinates, or when benchmarking an accessible-surface-area implementation against the published Lee and Richards myoglobin values. Input is sequence-only (e.g. FASTA): geodesic integration needs 3D atomic coordinates, neighboring atoms, and van der Waals radii, and DSSP does not predict structure from sequence. The goal is secondary-structure assignment (turns/bridges/helices recognized from hydrogen-bond patterns) rather than solvent exposure — that is separate DSSP machinery. Trusted per-residue exposure values already exist in the DSSP database output for the PDB entry — recompute only when coordinates or radii change or when benchmarking. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Reconstructs DSSP-style static solvent exposure by rolling a water-probe sphere over geodesic test points (icosahedron subdivided to 80 or 320 points) on each atom, counting unobstructed directions into per-residue accessible area, and validating against the published Lee and Richards myoglobin values (tolerance <=4 A^2 at 80 points, <=1 A^2 at 320 points). DSSP reports this exposure as the number of water molecules in possible contact with a residue. proteomics/v1 10.1002/bip.360221211
skills.summary: Reconstructs DSSP-style static solvent exposure by rolling a water-probe sphere over geodesic test points (icosahedron subdivided to 80 or 320 points) on each atom, counting unobstructed directions into per-residue accessible area, and validating against the published Lee and Richards myoglobin values (tolerance <=4 A^2 at 80 points, <=1 A^2 at 320 points). DSSP reports this exposure as the number of water molecules in possible contact with a residue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is sequence-only (e.g. FASTA): geodesic integration needs 3D atomic coordinates, neighboring atoms, and van der Waals radii, and DSSP does not predict structure from sequence. The goal is secondary-structure assignment (turns/bridges/helices recognized from hydrogen-bond patterns) rather than solvent exposure — that is separate DSSP machinery. Trusted per-residue exposure values already exist in the DSSP database output for the PDB entry — recompute only when coordinates or radii change or when benchmarking.

skills.search_text: targeted-proteomics-assay-validation Use when a dilution/concentration series of replicate measurements (e.g., transition-level intensities from an Agilent 6490 MRM run or msqc1 data) must be converted into a validated calibration curve with a defensible linear range and quantification limits. The data are not replicate measurements over a concentration/dilution series (e.g., a single concentration or a global (shotgun) proteomics experiment), since no linear range or PB metrics can be determined You only need to report R² of a single fit without assessing trueness — the article explicitly shows R² alone is misleading for comparing unweighted vs weighted calibration models You require the legacy KNIME workflow: development of the KNIME-based version was discontinued and replaced by the R package and Nextflow workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Validate targeted MS (SRM/MRM/PRM) quantitative assays by fitting weighted and unweighted calibration curves over dilution series with CalibraCurve, determining the final linear range (LLOQ/ULOQ) via PB_av/PB_cv thresholds, and judging fits by precision- and trueness-based measures rather than R² alone. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201900143
skills.summary: Validate targeted MS (SRM/MRM/PRM) quantitative assays by fitting weighted and unweighted calibration curves over dilution series with CalibraCurve, determining the final linear range (LLOQ/ULOQ) via PB_av/PB_cv thresholds, and judging fits by precision- and trueness-based measures rather than R² alone.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not replicate measurements over a concentration/dilution series (e.g., a single concentration or a global (shotgun) proteomics experiment), since no linear range or PB metrics can be determined You only need to report R² of a single fit without assessing trueness — the article explicitly shows R² alone is misleading for comparing unweighted vs weighted calibration models You require the legacy KNIME workflow: development of the KNIME-based version was discontinued and replaced by the R package and Nextflow workflow

skills.description: Use when concentration/dilution-series data from targeted MS (SRM/MRM or PRM, e.g., msqc1 heavy/light peptide peak areas) must be converted into calibration curves with LLOQ/ULOQ and linear-range estimates, or compared across instruments.
skills.name: targeted-proteomics-calibration-curve-fitting
skills.search_text: targeted-proteomics-calibration-curve-fitting Use when concentration/dilution-series data from targeted MS (SRM/MRM or PRM, e.g., msqc1 heavy/light peptide peak areas) must be converted into calibration curves with LLOQ/ULOQ and linear-range estimates, or compared across instruments. Data are not from a dilution/concentration series with known analyte amounts (CalibraCurve relies on known concentrations to fit calibration curves) The goal is global/shotgun proteomics quantification rather than targeted (SRM/MRM or PRM) assay calibration Only raw instrument files need inspection without curve fitting — raw data inspection is done with Skyline, not CalibraCurve http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Fits calibration curves to targeted-MS dilution-series data (e.g., msqc1 heavy/light peptide peak areas) using CalibraCurve to determine dynamic linear ranges, quantification limits, and R-squared quality of fit per instrument, enabling cross-instrument benchmarking. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201900143
skills.summary: Fits calibration curves to targeted-MS dilution-series data (e.g., msqc1 heavy/light peptide peak areas) using CalibraCurve to determine dynamic linear ranges, quantification limits, and R-squared quality of fit per instrument, enabling cross-instrument benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not from a dilution/concentration series with known analyte amounts (CalibraCurve relies on known concentrations to fit calibration curves) The goal is global/shotgun proteomics quantification rather than targeted (SRM/MRM or PRM) assay calibration Only raw instrument files need inspection without curve fitting — raw data inspection is done with Skyline, not CalibraCurve

skills.description: Use when a replicate intensity table from a concentration or dilution series (e.g. msqc1 calibration data) must be reduced to a linear quantification range via per-level replicate CV against a threshold TMeasCV.
skills.name: targeted-proteomics-dilution-series-analysis
skills.search_text: targeted-proteomics-dilution-series-analysis Use when a replicate intensity table from a concentration or dilution series (e.g. msqc1 calibration data) must be reduced to a linear quantification range via per-level replicate CV against a threshold TMeasCV. Input is already a fitted calibration curve or a summary statistics table — MeasCV must be recomputed from replicate intensities per concentration level Data are shotgun (DDA) proteomics measurements rather than targeted SRM/MRM/PRM dilution-series replicates, for which the paper's dynamic-range framing does not apply The goal is ULOQ determination from signal reduction at high analyte concentrations without replicate-level CV computation http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Reconstructs CalibraCurve's preliminary linear range (PLR) computation from per-concentration-level MeasCV values and a user-defined threshold TMeasCV, enabling determination of dynamic linear ranges and quantification limits for targeted MS (SRM/MRM, PRM) dilution-series data. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201900143
skills.summary: Reconstructs CalibraCurve's preliminary linear range (PLR) computation from per-concentration-level MeasCV values and a user-defined threshold TMeasCV, enabling determination of dynamic linear ranges and quantification limits for targeted MS (SRM/MRM, PRM) dilution-series data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fitted calibration curve or a summary statistics table — MeasCV must be recomputed from replicate intensities per concentration level Data are shotgun (DDA) proteomics measurements rather than targeted SRM/MRM/PRM dilution-series replicates, for which the paper's dynamic-range framing does not apply The goal is ULOQ determination from signal reduction at high analyte concentrations without replicate-level CV computation

skills.description: Use when targeted MS (SRM/MRM or PRM) calibration data from concentration or dilution series with known analyte amounts must yield an automated linear range (LLOQ/ULOQ) and fitted calibration curves for downstream concentration prediction.
skills.name: targeted-proteomics-linear-range-output
skills.search_text: targeted-proteomics-linear-range-output Use when targeted MS (SRM/MRM or PRM) calibration data from concentration or dilution series with known analyte amounts must yield an automated linear range (LLOQ/ULOQ) and fitted calibration curves for downstream concentration prediction. Data are from classical shotgun (DDA) proteomics rather than targeted SRM/MRM or PRM assays, where the calibration-based linear range concept does not apply the same way The calibration relationship must hold across the full concentration span with no linear range restriction — CalibraCurve explicitly models the region where linearity breaks down (e.g. reduced product ion intensities at higher analyte concentrations) Raw MS data inspection is the goal (use Skyline); CalibraCurve operates on curve-fitting/calibration data, not raw spectra http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Determines the dynamic linear range (lower and upper limits of quantification) of targeted MS-based (SRM/MRM, PRM) assays from dilution-series calibration data using CalibraCurve, and emits fitted weighted/unweighted calibration models plus calibration curve and response factor plot outputs for assessing precision and trueness. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201900143
skills.summary: Determines the dynamic linear range (lower and upper limits of quantification) of targeted MS-based (SRM/MRM, PRM) assays from dilution-series calibration data using CalibraCurve, and emits fitted weighted/unweighted calibration models plus calibration curve and response factor plot outputs for assessing precision and trueness.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are from classical shotgun (DDA) proteomics rather than targeted SRM/MRM or PRM assays, where the calibration-based linear range concept does not apply the same way The calibration relationship must hold across the full concentration span with no linear range restriction — CalibraCurve explicitly models the region where linearity breaks down (e.g. reduced product ion intensities at higher analyte concentrations) Raw MS data inspection is the goal (use Skyline); CalibraCurve operates on curve-fitting/calibration data, not raw spectra

skills.description: Use when a FT-ICR MS molecular compositional table sampled across multiple temperature levels (e.g., six levels in temperate and subtropical regions) must be tested for significant diversity-temperature trends.
skills.name: temperature-gradient-trend-regression
skills.search_text: temperature-gradient-trend-regression Use when a FT-ICR MS molecular compositional table sampled across multiple temperature levels (e.g., six levels in temperate and subtropical regions) must be tested for significant diversity-temperature trends. The data are already a taxon/OTU feature table rather than an FT-ICR MS molecular compositional table — this skill targets DOM molecules, not taxonomy Temperature is not a designed experimental gradient (no replicate levels), so a linear regression against temperature level is not meaningful The goal is quantifying assembly processes or dark-matter effects rather than testing thermal response trends — use commProc or iDME instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Fits linear regressions of DOM molecular diversity indices (richness, Shannon, evenness, RaoQ functional diversity, MNTD) against experimental temperature levels, separately per region (temperate vs subtropical), to test whether dissolved organic matter molecular richness changes significantly with warming. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mlf2.70002
skills.summary: Fits linear regressions of DOM molecular diversity indices (richness, Shannon, evenness, RaoQ functional diversity, MNTD) against experimental temperature levels, separately per region (temperate vs subtropical), to test whether dissolved organic matter molecular richness changes significantly with warming.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already a taxon/OTU feature table rather than an FT-ICR MS molecular compositional table — this skill targets DOM molecules, not taxonomy Temperature is not a designed experimental gradient (no replicate levels), so a linear regression against temperature level is not meaningful The goal is quantifying assembly processes or dark-matter effects rather than testing thermal response trends — use commProc or iDME instead

skills.description: Use when training a 3D conditional GAN (e.g., SC-GAN) in TensorFlow on 256x256x256 multimodal MRI volumes to synthesize PET, FA, or MD maps, or when GPU memory constraints force batch size 1 and stabilized training (spectral normalization, feature matching) is needed.
skills.name: tensorflow-gpu-distributed-training
skills.search_text: tensorflow-gpu-distributed-training Use when training a 3D conditional GAN (e.g., SC-GAN) in TensorFlow on 256x256x256 multimodal MRI volumes to synthesize PET, FA, or MD maps, or when GPU memory constraints force batch size 1 and stabilized training (spectral normalization, feature matching) is needed. Synthesizing quantitative modalities (e.g., DTI metrics) where the 0-1 normalization step would negatively affect the quantitative value of the resulting metrics Multidimensional diffusion MRI superresolution tasks lacking the additional acquisition protocol data required for further experiments and analyses When GPU memory is insufficient: SC-GAN on 256^3 volumes requires heavy GPU resources, so without adequate hardware training is impractical http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3384 GPU-based TensorFlow training of the SC-GAN 3D self-attention conditional GAN (with spectral normalization and feature matching) for end-to-end synthesis of 256x256x256 neuroimaging volumes such as PET from multimodal MRI, plus tuned baselines (2D cGAN, 3D cGAN, Att cGAN) for benchmarking. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mrm.28819
skills.summary: GPU-based TensorFlow training of the SC-GAN 3D self-attention conditional GAN (with spectral normalization and feature matching) for end-to-end synthesis of 256x256x256 neuroimaging volumes such as PET from multimodal MRI, plus tuned baselines (2D cGAN, 3D cGAN, Att cGAN) for benchmarking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Synthesizing quantitative modalities (e.g., DTI metrics) where the 0-1 normalization step would negatively affect the quantitative value of the resulting metrics Multidimensional diffusion MRI superresolution tasks lacking the additional acquisition protocol data required for further experiments and analyses When GPU memory is insufficient: SC-GAN on 256^3 volumes requires heavy GPU resources, so without adequate hardware training is impractical

skills.description: Use when a paper's neural architecture (e.g. SC-GAN: 3D cGAN + self-attention + spectral normalization) has been reimplemented and you must verify the model graph constructs correctly and matches a reference implementation.
skills.name: tensorflow-model-instantiation-verification
skills.search_text: tensorflow-model-instantiation-verification Use when a paper's neural architecture (e.g. SC-GAN: 3D cGAN + self-attention + spectral normalization) has been reimplemented and you must verify the model graph constructs correctly and matches a reference implementation. The goal is to train or evaluate synthesis quality (normalized RMS error, PSNR, SSIM) — this skill only verifies graph construction, not prediction accuracy The model being verified is 2D or a different architecture (e.g. 3D Unet, plain 3D conditional GAN) whose layer topology differs from SC-GAN's self-attention 3D cGAN The reference implementation is unavailable, since structural comparison against the released SC-GAN code is a required validation step http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3304 A structural verification skill for a reimplemented TensorFlow model: instantiate the full SC-GAN generator/discriminator (3D conditional GAN with self-attention and spectral normalization) at the paper's configuration (batch size 1, 256×256×256) to confirm all layers, attention blocks, and loss terms build without error before any training is attempted. proteomics/v1 10.1002/mrm.28819
skills.summary: A structural verification skill for a reimplemented TensorFlow model: instantiate the full SC-GAN generator/discriminator (3D conditional GAN with self-attention and spectral normalization) at the paper's configuration (batch size 1, 256×256×256) to confirm all layers, attention blocks, and loss terms build without error before any training is attempted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to train or evaluate synthesis quality (normalized RMS error, PSNR, SSIM) — this skill only verifies graph construction, not prediction accuracy The model being verified is 2D or a different architecture (e.g. 3D Unet, plain 3D conditional GAN) whose layer topology differs from SC-GAN's self-attention 3D cGAN The reference implementation is unavailable, since structural comparison against the released SC-GAN code is a required validation step

skills.description: Use when candidate theoretical peptides from a sequence database must be scored against an MS/MS spectrum — especially for peptides carrying mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications.
skills.name: theoretical-fragment-ion-matching
skills.search_text: theoretical-fragment-ion-matching Use when candidate theoretical peptides from a sequence database must be scored against an MS/MS spectrum — especially for peptides carrying mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications. The goal is de novo sequencing without a peptide database — Popitam's identification process matches theoretical peptide sequences issued from a database, so it is the wrong choice when no candidate sequences exist You only need the spectrum graph construction or the ACO graph-parsing step and have no theoretical sequences to score yet — use those upstream skills instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Matches theoretical peptide sequences issued from a peptide database search against a structured representation (spectrum graph) of the source MS/MS spectrum, computing a correlation score of how well ACO-parsed graph sections align with each theoretical peptide, and outputs peptides ranked by that score. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.200300402
skills.summary: Matches theoretical peptide sequences issued from a peptide database search against a structured representation (spectrum graph) of the source MS/MS spectrum, computing a correlation score of how well ACO-parsed graph sections align with each theoretical peptide, and outputs peptides ranked by that score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo sequencing without a peptide database — Popitam's identification process matches theoretical peptide sequences issued from a database, so it is the wrong choice when no candidate sequences exist You only need the spectrum graph construction or the ACO graph-parsing step and have no theoretical sequences to score yet — use those upstream skills instead

skills.description: Use when identifying peptides from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data by database search, especially when mutations or unexpected PTMs are expected or the spectrum is of low quality.
skills.name: theoretical-peptide-sequence-matching
skills.search_text: theoretical-peptide-sequence-matching Use when identifying peptides from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data by database search, especially when mutations or unexpected PTMs are expected or the spectrum is of low quality. The input is raw MS/MS spectra that have not yet been converted into a spectrum-graph representation — build the graph representation first. The goal is purely de novo sequencing without a peptide sequence database — Popitam's matching is database-search based, though its graph representation resembles de novo spectrum graphs. No candidate theoretical sequences are available; the ACO parsing emphasizes graph sections relative to each theoretical sequence and cannot run without them. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Matches theoretical peptide sequences from a sequence database against a spectrum-graph representation of an MS/MS spectrum using Popitam's Ant Colony Optimization parsing, producing peptides ranked by a correlation score. This handles the combinatorial complexity of the graph, including peptides carrying mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.200300402
skills.summary: Matches theoretical peptide sequences from a sequence database against a spectrum-graph representation of an MS/MS spectrum using Popitam's Ant Colony Optimization parsing, producing peptides ranked by a correlation score. This handles the combinatorial complexity of the graph, including peptides carrying mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw MS/MS spectra that have not yet been converted into a spectrum-graph representation — build the graph representation first. The goal is purely de novo sequencing without a peptide sequence database — Popitam's matching is database-search based, though its graph representation resembles de novo spectrum graphs. No candidate theoretical sequences are available; the ACO parsing emphasizes graph sections relative to each theoretical sequence and cannot run without them.

skills.description: Use when automating DSF Tm screening over many melting curves and needing rules to accept secondary Tms, reject noisy peaks, flag uninterpretable curves, or detect pre-denatured samples.
skills.name: thermal-denaturation-curve-classification
skills.search_text: thermal-denaturation-curve-classification Use when automating DSF Tm screening over many melting curves and needing rules to accept secondary Tms, reject noisy peaks, flag uninterpretable curves, or detect pre-denatured samples. The FDCs have not been normalized and smoothed first — raw derivative curves will produce noise peaks that fail or corrupt the 10% threshold logic Curves with 3 recognized peaks fall in a gap between the two-peak (dual Tm) and >=4-peak (no Tm) rules; interpret these manually rather than trusting the automated flag http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Automated classification of DSF melting curves using peak finding on normalized, smoothed first derivative curves (FDCs): peaks must exceed 10% of the highest peak's width and height to qualify, >=4 qualifying peaks flag 'no Tm calculated', and declining MCs are classified as unfolded/denatured with the initial temperature reported. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pro.3703
skills.summary: Automated classification of DSF melting curves using peak finding on normalized, smoothed first derivative curves (FDCs): peaks must exceed 10% of the highest peak's width and height to qualify, >=4 qualifying peaks flag 'no Tm calculated', and declining MCs are classified as unfolded/denatured with the initial temperature reported.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The FDCs have not been normalized and smoothed first — raw derivative curves will produce noise peaks that fail or corrupt the 10% threshold logic Curves with 3 recognized peaks fall in a gap between the two-peak (dual Tm) and >=4-peak (no Tm) rules; interpret these manually rather than trusting the automated flag

skills.description: Use when reprocessing TMTpro isobaric-labeled PISA/thermal-proteome raw data (e.g., PRIDE PXD014369) to compare unfiltered vs. QC-filtered protein quantification and count significant thermal-shift drug targets.
skills.name: thermal-proteome-profiling-analysis
skills.search_text: thermal-proteome-profiling-analysis Use when reprocessing TMTpro isobaric-labeled PISA/thermal-proteome raw data (e.g., PRIDE PXD014369) to compare unfiltered vs. QC-filtered protein quantification and count significant thermal-shift drug targets. Input data were acquired with RTS-MS3 limited to a maximum of 2 PSMs per protein, which significantly limits the possibility of filtering peptides The goal is cross-run normalization or downstream statistical modeling of an existing protein-level table rather than scan-level isobaric quantification and QC filtering The labeling scheme exceeds IsobaricQuant support (iTRAQ up to 8-plex, TMT up to 11-plex, TMTpro up to 16-plex) or the data are not isobarically labeled http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Reproduces the IsobaricQuant-based PISA thermal-shift workflow (PXD014369, staurosporine), in which TMTpro-labeled MS2- and RTS-MS3-acquired PISA data are quantified, QC-score-filtered (PeptideTopXIntensityFromTotalScore, cutoff 0.15, topX=10), and aggregated to protein level to improve sensitivity of kinase-inhibitor target identification. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.202100253
skills.summary: Reproduces the IsobaricQuant-based PISA thermal-shift workflow (PXD014369, staurosporine), in which TMTpro-labeled MS2- and RTS-MS3-acquired PISA data are quantified, QC-score-filtered (PeptideTopXIntensityFromTotalScore, cutoff 0.15, topX=10), and aggregated to protein level to improve sensitivity of kinase-inhibitor target identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data were acquired with RTS-MS3 limited to a maximum of 2 PSMs per protein, which significantly limits the possibility of filtering peptides The goal is cross-run normalization or downstream statistical modeling of an existing protein-level table rather than scan-level isobaric quantification and QC filtering The labeling scheme exceeds IsobaricQuant support (iTRAQ up to 8-plex, TMT up to 11-plex, TMTpro up to 16-plex) or the data are not isobarically labeled

skills.description: Use when isobarically-labeled (TMT/TMTpro/iTRAQ) MS2 or RTS-MS3 reporter-ion quantifications suffer precursor interference (ratio compression) and you want to filter inaccurate scans with QC score cutoffs before protein-level quantification.
skills.name: tmt-interference-qc-score-filtering
skills.search_text: tmt-interference-qc-score-filtering Use when isobarically-labeled (TMT/TMTpro/iTRAQ) MS2 or RTS-MS3 reporter-ion quantifications suffer precursor interference (ratio compression) and you want to filter inaccurate scans with QC score cutoffs before protein-level quantification. Data are label-free or otherwise not isobarically tagged (iTRAQ/TMT/TMTpro) — IsobaricQuant scores address reporter-ion co-isolation interference Quantification is already at RTS-MS3 acquisition with only ~2 PSMs per protein, where filtering possibilities are severely limited You need every peptide observation and cannot tolerate increased missing values — stringent filtering significantly decreases peptide observations http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Filter co-isolation-interfered TMT/TMTpro/iTRAQ peptide quantifications using IsobaricQuant QC scores (e.g. peptideTopXIntensityFromTotalScore, peptideIntensityScore, msnTotalSignal) applied prior to protein-level aggregation, improving quantitative accuracy and target sensitivity while preserving protein depth. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.202100253
skills.summary: Filter co-isolation-interfered TMT/TMTpro/iTRAQ peptide quantifications using IsobaricQuant QC scores (e.g. peptideTopXIntensityFromTotalScore, peptideIntensityScore, msnTotalSignal) applied prior to protein-level aggregation, improving quantitative accuracy and target sensitivity while preserving protein depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are label-free or otherwise not isobarically tagged (iTRAQ/TMT/TMTpro) — IsobaricQuant scores address reporter-ion co-isolation interference Quantification is already at RTS-MS3 acquisition with only ~2 PSMs per protein, where filtering possibilities are severely limited You need every peptide observation and cannot tolerate increased missing values — stringent filtering significantly decreases peptide observations

skills.description: Use when you have TMT reporter-ion intensities from a labelled MS experiment and need per-feature log2 channel ratios (M) versus mean log2 intensity (A) plotted as MA plots, e.g. to visualise ratio spread between reporter channels.
skills.name: tmt-reporter-channel-ratio-analysis
skills.search_text: tmt-reporter-channel-ratio-analysis Use when you have TMT reporter-ion intensities from a labelled MS experiment and need per-feature log2 channel ratios (M) versus mean log2 intensity (A) plotted as MA plots, e.g. to visualise ratio spread between reporter channels. The input is already a processed feature table with pre-computed fold-changes and no reporter-channel intensities to re-derive M and A from The experiment is label-free or uses a different labelling scheme (e.g. SILAC) where TMT reporter-ion channel ratios do not apply The goal is quantitative statistical testing of channel differences rather than qualitative visualisation with R's plotting systems http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Computes per-feature M (log2 intensity ratio of a TMT reporter channel over a reference channel) and A (mean log2 reporter intensity) values from a TMT 6-plex experiment (PXD000001, HeLa/PRTC on a Thermo Orbitrap Q Exactive) and renders MA plots with R's traditional, lattice and ggplot2 plotting systems, as in Figure 1 of Gatto et al. 2015. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201400392
skills.summary: Computes per-feature M (log2 intensity ratio of a TMT reporter channel over a reference channel) and A (mean log2 reporter intensity) values from a TMT 6-plex experiment (PXD000001, HeLa/PRTC on a Thermo Orbitrap Q Exactive) and renders MA plots with R's traditional, lattice and ggplot2 plotting systems, as in Figure 1 of Gatto et al. 2015.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a processed feature table with pre-computed fold-changes and no reporter-channel intensities to re-derive M and A from The experiment is label-free or uses a different labelling scheme (e.g. SILAC) where TMT reporter-ion channel ratios do not apply The goal is quantitative statistical testing of channel differences rather than qualitative visualisation with R's plotting systems

skills.name: uloq-out-of-range-prediction-flagging
skills.search_text: uloq-out-of-range-prediction-flagging Use when new intensity values from an SRM/MRM or PRM targeted MS assay (e.g. msqc1 dilution-series data) must be converted to concentrations with a fitted CalibraCurve model, and out-of-linear-range values must be flagged. skills.search_text: umap-dimensionality-reduction Use when you need a 2D visual check that a selected feature subset (e.g., LGBM-ranked features from fused BiLSTM 3605D + UniRep 1900D embeddings) separates two protein classes before or after classifier training. skills.description: Use when reproducing the Figure 4 runtime scaling evaluation: six HLA search-result datasets of varying PSM counts need per-step (conversion, prediction, rescoring) and total wall-clock timings to test linear scaling with PSM count.
skills.name: wallclock-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: wallclock-runtime-benchmarking Use when reproducing the Figure 4 runtime scaling evaluation: six HLA search-result datasets of varying PSM counts need per-step (conversion, prediction, rescoring) and total wall-clock timings to test linear scaling with PSM count. The goal is identification performance (FDR, gain in identifications) rather than computational cost — this skill times steps only and does not evaluate rescoring sensitivity. The input is not search-engine PSM results plus RAW spectra (e.g. already-rescored mzIdentML or a spectral-library job type such as 'SpectralLibraryGeneration' or 'CollisionEnergCalibration'). Only a single small dataset is available — linear scaling and the ~4x speedup claim require multiple PSM-count conditions to be verifiable. http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 Times each step and the total wall-clock duration of Oktoberfest's data-driven rescoring pipeline across HLA raw-file combinations of increasing PSM counts, to characterize how runtime scales with input size (linear scaling in Figure 4) and quantify the multi-processing speedup. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.202300112
skills.summary: Times each step and the total wall-clock duration of Oktoberfest's data-driven rescoring pipeline across HLA raw-file combinations of increasing PSM counts, to characterize how runtime scales with input size (linear scaling in Figure 4) and quantify the multi-processing speedup.

skills.description: Use when you need to convert protein/GPCR primary sequences into fixed-length word-embedding features by splitting them into l-mers (l=2,3,4), training CBOW models on the resulting wordbooks, and aggregating word vectors per sequence.
skills.name: word2vec-cbow-model-training
skills.search_text: word2vec-cbow-model-training Use when you need to convert protein/GPCR primary sequences into fixed-length word-embedding features by splitting them into l-mers (l=2,3,4), training CBOW models on the resulting wordbooks, and aggregating word vectors per sequence. The input is already a numeric feature table (e.g., precomputed BOW or embedding features) — training CBOW models would be redundant; go straight to the downstream DL/XGBoost pipeline. The task is purely classifier selection (CatBoost vs XGBoost) rather than feature extraction — the embedding step produces only the original features that are fed onward. Sequences are not protein primary sequences (e.g., nucleotide or short peptides outside the GPCR fragment-length regime), so the l=2/3/4 wordbook assumptions do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train Gensim Word2vec Continuous Bag-of-Words (CBOW) models with Negative Sampling on amino-acid fragment wordbooks of a GPCR sequence set, then use the trained models to embed each sequence into word-embedding features (EF2, EF3, EF4) that are concatenated into a fixed-length 896-D WEF vector. proteomics/v1 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.08.044
skills.summary: Train Gensim Word2vec Continuous Bag-of-Words (CBOW) models with Negative Sampling on amino-acid fragment wordbooks of a GPCR sequence set, then use the trained models to embed each sequence into word-embedding features (EF2, EF3, EF4) that are concatenated into a fixed-length 896-D WEF vector.

skills.search_text: wt-vs-knockout-ptm-comparison Use when two genotypes (e.g., wt vs a knockout like Suz12-/-) have been quantified for combinatorial histone marks in more than one histone preparation (purified H3 vs crude mixture), and you must test which binary marks change significantly and whether the preparations agree. Data are bottom-up tryptic histone peptides rather than middle-down histone tails — isoScale quantification via FIRR is recommended specifically for middle-down or top-down analyses comparing single sequences with scrambled combinatorial PTMs. Input is still raw Mascot output in .xml — that must first be processed by Histone Coder (localization validation and Brno nomenclature conversion) before binary-mark abundance comparison. The question concerns single PTMs or three-plus-mark combinatorial states rather than co-existing binary (two-mark) marks — this skill's t-test and concordance validation are defined on binary marks only. http://edamontology.org/topic_0121 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Cross-preparation comparison of co-existing binary histone PTM mark abundances between wild-type and Suz12-/- murine ESCs, testing whether significant genotype differences agree between purified histone H3 (higher sensitivity) and crude histone mixture preparations analyzed by middle-down LC-MS/MS with Histone Coder and isoScale. proteomics/v1 10.1002/pmic.201400084

The task is quantification of absolute metabolite concentrations in vivo — Bloch-McConnell based quantification is described as extremely challenging in vivo and is beyond this skill's scope.
